comments.content: Returning `done` bypasses the before/after workspace check in `coherently` (it returns immediately for this branch). Consequently, `checkBinding` is not actually a coherent read: for example, a new eligible trade/instrument inserted after `eligibleTrades` can be omitted from the frame request, letting the old snapshot match and the save succeed. Return successful validation through `settle` so changes during assembly trigger a bounded retry.
comments.existing_code: return { done: { kind: 'Checked', cutoff: session.closeInstant, marks } };

comments.content: These checks protect only review-date rows, but `ResolveFrames` also includes the historical stale mark's revision ID in its snapshot when the review-date price is missing. Correcting that earlier mark after `checkBinding` and before commit changes the evidence shown on the form without changing any of these rows, so the action is saved against stale evidence instead of returning `ReviewChanged`. Protect historical frame dependencies too (or require an appropriate snapshot-wide revision and retry), and add a race test for correcting the stale-context mark.

This unbound read can return a different writer's action rather than the action just committed. Another save can read and edit the newly committed entry before this query runs; `MutationGuard.run` does not serialize writers. The original Hold save could then report `Saved` with the other writer's Exit and revision. Build the returned action from the staged/committed entry and its exact revision, rather than querying the latest action after commit.

A failure in this post-commit refresh escapes into MutationGuard.run, which returns StorageFailure (or RuntimeNotWritable), even though the Action has already been committed. Those failure results imply nothing was written; retrying a new Action with the original binding then produces Conflict. Keep post-commit refresh failures separate from mutation failures and preserve the Saved outcome, using the committed Action and a ChangedDuringAssembly review when the refresh cannot be obtained. The preceding queryActions read needs the same protection.
comments.existing_code: return { kind: 'Saved', action, review: await postSaveReview(binding.reviewDate) };
